observation: Design-it-twice section prevented schema migration bugs — two CRITICAL findings (seedBuiltinRoutines FK violation and team_id NOT NULL ordering) were caught at critique, before any code was written. Critique score 7/10; builder avoided implementing two known blockers.

Design-variant approval process worked — designer produced 2 variants (Variant A rejected 64/90, Variant B approved). Builder initially implemented Variant A pattern (card-per-row) despite Variant B approval. Design review round 1 caught the mismatch. Builder re-implemented in fix cycle (2 commits) to match Variant B (flat status table). Zero regression on Variant B design after fix.

Design-variant mismatch in initial implementation — builder read the approval doc but produced the rejected design pattern anyway. Possible causes: (1) visual mockup less clear than verbal spec, (2) pattern matching to existing BetCard rather than following architecture plan, (3) no pre-implementation design review between designer-approved.md and write-code.

Review round 1 found 8 findings (5 MUST FIX, 3 SHOULD FIX) before CI passed — design mismatch, missing detail-page content, missing run history limit, incomplete KV grid, stale @ts-expect-error, N+1 query, missing action buttons, portfolio text deviation. All 8 were fixable; only 2 review rounds needed (Round 1 + Round 2 verification).

Cost signal: 15 feature commits (54 files, 8569 insertions) with 2 review rounds and 1 fix cycle. Productive commits (feat + test): 8. CI/orchestration/documentation commits: 7 (47%). Rework/fix commits: 2 (after review round 1). Average: 5.5 days per phase (concept + design + arch + review critique + build + code review + rework + ship).

Protected tests required explicit attention — migration added NOT NULL teamId to routines table. Architecture plan Task 10 identified test files needing updates but did not list seedBuiltinRoutines in @hyperidle/fabric. Builder found and fixed this during implementation, but it was a trip-hazard flagged only at critique level (Failure-Mode Coverage: 6/10 because seedBuiltinRoutines gap was not named explicitly).

Architecture plan's plan-reconciliation section was load-bearing — table in section 'Plan reconciliation: spec vs reality' caught 8 spec-vs-reality gaps upfront (no name column, no team_id, boolean active vs tri-state state, COS/PF agents, no routine_runs table, no createdAt, no team-scoped API, no /work/routine/:id route). Zero surprise gaps during build.

TDD red/green phases strict — builder wrote failing tests for all 6 ACs before implementation. 60+ test cases across 4 test files. Tests passed on first implementation run. Zero test-writing debt at review time.
